question.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10 \\ -12\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ -16\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Assume that ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers. Which of the following statements are true?

I. The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has only the trivial solution ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$

II. The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly dependent.

III. The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent.
question.worked_solution:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}+8{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}-16{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 3 & 10 & 8 & 0 \\ -4 & -12 & -16 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & -12 & -16 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we conclude that the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, while ${x}_{3}$ is the free variable. 

Since there is one free variable, the equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has an infinite number of nonzero solutions, which means that the vectors are linearly dependent. 

Therefore, statements I and III are false, while statement II is true.
